problems.where: S1-O2 (fluency), contrast GenAI vs Baseline (No support), and open_questions[2]
problems.field: contrasts[0].reported; open_questions[2]; notes (list of printed inconsistencies)
problems.form_value: open_questions[2]: 'Arm-level values appear only as plotted posterior predictions in Figures 6-9, so participant-level means and SDs for standardization are not printed'. S1-O2 'reported' gives only Table 2 and says Figure 7 has no printed values. The notes list printed inconsistencies but not this one.
problems.source_says: The paper prints the GenAI arm's sketch total: 92 sketches from 20 participants, a mean fluency of 4.6 (p. 12). Table 2's total-effects model implies exp(1.50 - .21) = 3.63 sketches for GenAI, and Figure 7 plots GenAI at about 3.6. Across arms the model implies 20 x (4.48 + 2.75 + 3.63) = 217 sketches, but p. 5 prints N = 277. Both gaps equal one sketch per participant (92 - 20 = 72 = 20 x 3.6, and 277 - 60 = 217). With weakly informative priors, a negative binomial model with a log link reproduces each arm's mean count, so the prior cannot explain the gap. The pattern fits a fluency model fitted to sketches minus one, as the variety model is, but the paper does not say so: Eq. 2 and the Figure 7 axis say 'number of sketches'. So the form's claim that no arm level is printed is wrong for GenAI fluency, and the conflict is missing from 'reported' and from the notes. Fix: record the 92-sketch total (4.6 per GenAI participant) in S1-O2 'reported', add the conflict to the notes, and correct open_questions[2]. Extraction should not read Table 2 as a ratio of sketch counts until this is resolved. No code changes: no_clear_difference rests on the Table 2 interval, and the GenAI vs Image Search order rests on the Table 2 coefficients and the text.
problems.quote: For this analysis, we begin with the total set of sketches produced by participants in the AI condition (92 in total).
problems.locator: p. 12, Section 4.6.2 (92 GenAI sketches); p. 9, Table 2 (Total Effects) and Figure 7; p. 5, Section 3.1 (N=277 sketches; Eq. 2)

problems.form_value: notes: 'Figures 6-9 plot posterior predictions on normalized scales, while the models use the original counts (p. 8).' open_questions[2]: 'Extraction would need to digitize the figures or ask the authors.'
problems.source_says: Figure 8 plots variety at about 0.080 (Baseline), 0.054 (Image Search), and 0.060 (GenAI) on an axis labeled 'Percentage of clusters'. On the Eq. 3 scale, which divides by 83 - 1 = 82, Table 3's total effects give exp(1.01)/82 = 0.034 (Baseline), 0.025 (GenAI), and 0.023 (Image Search). No arm can average above (277/60 - 1)/82 = 0.044 on that scale, because each sketch belongs to exactly one cluster. Every plotted level is about 2.4 times the Eq. 3 value. So the ratios between arms agree with Table 3, but the levels are not on the scale the paper says it plots. Figures 6, 7, and 9 do match their tables (Phi(-.71) = .24, exp(1.50) = 4.48, intercept .86). The form repeats the paper's claim about the scale and proposes digitizing Figures 6-9 for arm levels, with no warning about Figure 8. No code or recorded number changes.
problems.quote: We built our models based on the original count data in the direct measurements but report normalised values as described in Section 3.1 in our plots for easier comparisons with future work.
problems.locator: p. 8, Section 4.1; p. 9, Figure 8 and Table 3 (Total Effects); p. 5, Section 3.1 (Eq. 3, 83 clusters, N=277 sketches)

confirmed: Criterion 3 holds. All four outcomes are scored on the sketches, and none is self-reported. Two raters counted the example's features in each sketch (DFS, Eq. 1). Fluency counts each participant's sketches (Eq. 2). Variety and originality come from 83 clusters that two raters built from all 277 sketches (Eqs. 3-4) (p. 5, Section 3.1; p. 7, Section 3.4).

measure expert_raters for S1-O1 holds. The two evaluators who computed DFS, variety, and originality 'were researchers from the human-computer interaction domain with experience in teaching and evaluating design' (p. 7, Section 3.4). category_count fits S1-O2 to S1-O4: counts of sketches, of hand-built clusters, and of other participants per cluster. No inter-rater reliability value is printed. The only mention is 'We validated the ratings by computing the inter-rater reliability' (p. 5).

AI availability 'yes' and timing 'immediate' hold for all four outcomes. Midjourney was the 'Inspiration Stimulus available during the task', and 'These tools were available for them to use on an Apple MacBook M1 Pro laptop' during the 20-minute sketching. There is no later session (p. 4, Section 3.1; p. 6, Section 3.3). No construct is diversity, so with_ai is the codebook answer for every outcome.

Constructs hold. Fluency is the number of sketches (Eq. 2). For variety, 'Each participant received a Variety score based on the number of clusters their sketches were classified into', which is variety within one person, so flexibility. Originality is the rarity of one sketch among other participants' sketches, and the paper calls it 'Originality (also called Novelty', the codebook's novelty. Design fixation counts copied example features ('higher is worse'), so 'other' with a description holds (p. 5; p. 8, Figure 6 caption).

Units hold. DFS is 'an objective property of each sketch', and its model has participant and image random effects. Originality is modeled per sketch ('the same cluster as each sketch') with a participant random effect. Fluency and variety are counts per participant (p. 5; p. 8, Section 4.2 and Table 1; p. 9, Sections 4.3-4.4; p. 10, Section 4.5 and Table 4). As the form says, the paper does not state whether the DFS model has one row per sketch or one per rater.

Table 1 matches the form exactly: Intercept -.71 (.10) [-.86, .56], Image Search .27 (0.14) [.05, .48], GenAI .32 (0.13) [.11, .54]. The text matches too: 100 percent probability, [.11, .55], BF 124 for GenAI, and [.05, .49], 98 percent, BF 42.48 for Image Search (p. 8, Section 4.2).

Table 4 matches. Direct effects: Image Search -.01 (0.02) [-.03, .02], GenAI -.03 (0.02) [-.05, -.01]. Total effects: Intercept .86 (.01) [.84, .88], Image Search -.01 (.02) [-.04, .01], GenAI -.03 (.02) [-.06, -.01]. Text: [-.06, .00], 97 percent, BF 35; [-.04, .01], BF 3.9; 'these effects were negligible' (p. 10).

Directions hold. Each Bayes Factor the paper quotes equals p/(1 - p) for its stated posterior probability (3.20 and 76 percent, 46.62 and 98 percent, 5.93 and 86 percent, 35 and 97 percent). For originality, 97 percent negative leaves under 5.5 percent of the posterior above zero, so the 89 percent interval excludes zero and treatment_lower holds although the text prints [-.06, .00]. The GenAI fluency and variety intervals include zero, so no_clear_difference follows the form's stated rule. The GenAI vs Image Search orders follow the printed coefficients and the text (pp. 8-10).

Extraction note, not an error: Table 3's Image Search total interval [-.84, -.06] and the text's [-.87, -.07] are recorded as printed. With SD .28 and a Bayes Factor of 11.38 (about 92 percent probability negative, so about 8 percent of the posterior above zero), the upper bound must be positive, so both look like sign typos. No coded contrast uses this interval (p. 9).
Comparison types hold. 'Baseline: no inspiration support' gives ai_vs_bau. Image Search is Google Images in an incognito browser, a web search, so ai_vs_active (p. 4, Section 3.1).

No outcome that bears on the three questions is missing. The paper reports no similarity among different people's sketches within an arm and no session after AI is removed. The Spearman correlation (rho = 0.56, 82 sketches) is within the GenAI arm. The 44 percent (206/468) share describes Midjourney's images, and Table 5 describes prompts. NASA-TLX is self-reported workload (p. 6; pp. 11-12; Table A.1, p. 18).
As the form records, the conclusion's claim that GenAI gave lower fluency, variety, and originality than image search conflicts with Tables 2-3 on fluency and variety (p. 16, Section 6; p. 9).
summary: The core coding of c127 holds: all four outcomes (design fixation, fluency, variety, originality) are scored on sketches drawn with Midjourney available, the question, construct, measure, unit, and AI-availability codes follow the codebook, and every number in 'reported' matches Tables 1-4 and the text exactly. The conclusion is refuted on what the form says the paper prints, because p. 12 gives the GenAI arm's fluency total (92 sketches, 4.6 per participant), which contradicts Table 2 and Figure 7 (about 3.6) and the form's claim that no arm level is printed, and Figure 8's variety levels sit about 2.4 times above the Eq. 3 scale, a conflict the form does not flag although it proposes digitizing the figures.
